script.title: Why a Tycoon Rebuilt London Bridge in the Desert
sentences: London Bridge actually sits in the middle of the Arizona desert.
In 1968, developer Robert McCulloch bought the 1830s landmark for over two million dollars.
He needed people to buy property in his scorching, empty desert settlement.
Workers numbered every exterior granite block and shipped them through the Panama Canal.
Crews rebuilt the structure over dry ground between mainland Arizona and a peninsula.
Only after it was finished did they dredge water underneath the arches.
The bizarre gamble worked, and surging land sales fully recouped his investment.
That is one extreme way to sell real estate.
script.description:
In 1968, an American entrepreneur bought London Bridge and moved it to the Arizona desert.
Here is how one of history's wildest real estate stunts succeeded.
visuals: London Bridge Lake Havasu City reconstruction 1970
Robert P McCulloch London Bridge Lake Havasu
claims_en: London Bridge is located in Lake Havasu City, Arizona.
In 1968, developer Robert P. McCulloch purchased the 1830s London Bridge for approximately 2.46 million dollars.
McCulloch purchased the bridge to attract buyers to his planned desert community in Lake Havasu City.
The bridge's original granite facing stones were numbered, catalogued, and transported by ship through the Panama Canal.
The bridge was reconstructed on dry land between the Arizona mainland and the Pittsburgh Point peninsula.
The Bridgewater Channel Canal was dredged beneath the bridge only after reconstruction was completed.
Increased land sales following the bridge's reconstruction recouped all of McCulloch's purchase and shipping expenses.
